profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA
profile.summary:
🔥 Passionate for building meaningful products and delivering impactful results.

🧑🏻‍💻 I lead projects, advise cross-functional teams, contribute to team building, integrate new technologies, architect scalable systems, design intuitive UIs, and drive fast execution through hands-on coding.

✏️  As a self-directed learner, I’m always eager to embrace new challenges that push me to acquire new technical skills.

📍 I’ve lived in Guatemala 🇬🇹, South Korea 🇰🇷, and the United States 🇺🇸. As a trilingual professional fluent in English, Spanish, and Korean, I help bridge cultural gaps while fostering inclusive and collaborative environments.

volunteerExperiences.description:
• Developed a web app that makes information about Kashaya, an endangered indigenous language of California, accessible to tribal members and others who would like to learn about the language. 
• Collaborated with Dr. Gene Buckley from the Linguistics department for the design and implementation of the web app, and IT team for hosting and setting up the CI/CD pipeline.

Link to web app: https://kashaya.ling.upenn.edu/

Skills used: JavaScript · React.js · Material UI · HTML / CSS · Python · NumPy / Pandas · Git · AWS S3 · AWS CodeBuild / CodePipeline

Collaborated with Prof. Brandon Krakowsky and 9 other teaching assistants to lead CIT 590 - "Programming Languages and Techniques", using Java and Python, for a group of 110 students. Held weekly office hours and led recitations covering topics such as programming patterns (recursion, iteration, call-backs, map-reduce, etc.), data types and representation, basic data structures, object-oriented programming, and functional programming.

Skills used: Python, Java, Data Structures, Algorithms, Object-oriented Programming, Functional Programming

projects.title: SpotIt@Penn (PennApps XX Hackathon)
projects.description:
Skills: Python, JavaScript, React Native, Firebase(Auth, Firestore), spaCy-NLP, Scrapy-crawler, NoSQL
- Developed hybrid mobile application for both iOS and Android that aggregates a list of personalized events on campus aligned with users’ interests.
- Scraped over 300 on-campus events from Penn’s sub-domain websites using Scrapy, and automatically tagged interests associated with events using spaCy, a Natural Language Processing library.
- Designed/implemented NoSQL database for users and events data with Firestore; completed project in 48 hours.

projects.title: PennCloud
projects.description:
• Built distributed HTTP servers that handled client-side REST APIs with a load balancer using round robin routing
• Implemented SMTP and POP3 protocols from scratch for the webmail service.
• Developed backend key-value store similar to Google BigTable, with three replica nodes and data checkpoints for recovery
